bib.title: Inference Optimization (ch. 8, LLM Engineer's Handbook)
bib.venue: Packt, LLM Engineer's Handbook, ch. 8 (ISBN 9781836200079; read via O'Reilly)

question: Which techniques make LLM inference faster and smaller (KV cache, batching, speculative decoding, attention kernels, model parallelism, quantization), and how do TGI, vLLM and TensorRT-LLM support them?
contributions: Walks through static KV cache with torch.compile, continuous batching, speculative decoding, PagedAttention and FlashAttention-2 with transformers code
Explains data, pipeline and tensor parallelism and how to combine them
Covers PTQ vs QAT, absmax and zero-point INT8, LLM.int8(), NF4, GGUF/llama.cpp, GPTQ, EXL2, AWQ, QuIP#, HQQ, with Colab recipes
Compares TGI, vLLM and TensorRT-LLM feature support in Table 8.1

limits: Nearly every speedup or size figure comes with no model, hardware, batch size or workload.
Only measurement the chapter runs itself is the small speculative decoding demo, reported qualitatively as not significant; no timings or accuracy numbers anywhere.
Written in 2024: the framework comparison covers only TGI, vLLM and TensorRT-LLM and has dated.
The formula figures (KV cache size, absmax and zero-point equations) are images and do not appear in the text layer.
Medusa is described as enabling a 70M parameter model to approximate a 7B model, with no figure or setup.
practices: Use a static KV cache plus torch.compile (mode reduce-overhead, fullgraph=True) for decode speed where the architecture supports it (KV cache section).
Use continuous batching, native in TGI, vLLM and TensorRT-LLM, rather than waiting on the longest request; tune the waiting-served ratio (Continuous batching).
Use a draft model with the same tokenizer for speculative decoding, much smaller than the main model; use prompt lookup decoding for input-grounded tasks such as summarization (Speculative decoding).
Use FlashAttention-2 via attn_implementation in transformers; PagedAttention comes with vLLM, TGI and TensorRT-LLM (Optimized attention mechanisms).
Prefer pipeline and tensor parallelism for inference; data parallelism mainly serves training (Data parallelism).
Combine parallelisms: pipeline stages with tensor parallelism inside each stage; favour pipeline when memory is the constraint and tensor when latency is (Combining approaches).
Prefer BF16 over FP16 when hardware supports it (Ampere yes, Turing no) because networks need range more than precision (Introduction to quantization).
Use GGUF for CPU or mixed inference, EXL2/GPTQ for GPU-only speed, AWQ for broad engine support (quantization sections).

terms.definition: also known as in-flight batching, aims to prevent idle time by immediately feeding a new request into the batch as soon as one completes
also called assisted generation; uses spare compute capacity to predict multiple tokens simultaneously, using a smaller proxy model
a variant of speculative decoding tailored to input-grounded tasks like summarization where shared n-grams are used as the LLM candidate tokens
partitions the KV cache into blocks, eliminating the need for contiguous memory allocation
arise when some GPUs are idle, waiting for activations from preceding layers
the weights of a pre-trained model are directly converted to a lower precision format without any retraining
performs quantization during the training or fine-tuning stage, allowing the model to adapt to the lower precision weights
llama.cpp's own quantization format, designed to simplify and speed up model loading; files store tensors and metadata, from 1-bit to 8-bit
